subject: Close cadence: MSA/DPA orderform contingency & acceptance lanes (CardinalHealth)
messages:
From: Emma Liao <emma.liao@cardinalhealth.com>
To: markus_klein@redwood.com
Date: 2026-06-15T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: MAP & timeline proposal for pilot -> production (Cardinal)

Markus —

Thanks for the demo last week. We walked the team through the feature and there is strong interest to move our pilot (search + triage assistant) to a limited production run. Procurement asked me to put together a mutual action plan so legal and procurement can see the gating items and an estimated close cadence.

Quick summary of what Cardinal needs up front:
- MSA with standard indemnity + DPA (we have a few data residency questions)
- Order form that ties pilot pricing to committed throughput and an acceptance window (30 days)
- Evidence: SOC 2 report (latest), encryption at-rest/in-transit statement, and logging/audit details for request traces

Proposed MAP (we're flexible):
1) Week 0: Redwood sends MSA + DPA + Order Form draft
2) Week 1: Legal redlines + procurement questions
3) Week 2–3: Evidence exchange (SOC2 + security questionnaire)
4) Week 4: Pricing confirmation and sign-off (DocuSign)
5) Week 6: Pilot acceptance window closes; move to limited production

We can compress to 4 weeks if Redwood can commit to prioritizing DPA redlines (we have a compliance audit end of Q3). Attaching an initial MAP and SOC snapshot for your review. Please share who on your side will own DPA redlines and whether Redwood can provide an acceptance testing checklist that maps to order form criteria.

Thanks,
Emma

--
Emma Liao
Sr. Procurement Program Manager | CardinalHealth
emma.liao@cardinalhealth.com
attachments: Cardinal_MAP_v1.pdf, Cardinal_SOC2_Report_2025.pdf

From: markus_klein@redwood.com
To: Emma Liao <emma.liao@cardinalhealth.com>
Cc: karthik_iyer, irene_choi, olga_petrov
Date: 2026-06-15T11:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: MAP & timeline proposal for pilot -> production (Cardinal)

Emma —

Appreciate the clear MAP — this is exactly the level of detail that helps us prioritize. Short answers up front: we can meet the evidence+timeline but will need to sequence the legal work tightly so it doesn't block the SOC2 exchange or order form timing. Proposed sequencing from our side:

- Day 0: We will upload our standard MSA + DPA + Order Form draft (OrderForm_Draft_v3.docx attached).
- Day 1–3: Legal (Irene) triages DPA redline risk items and identifies must-haves vs. negotiables.
- Day 4–10: Procurement and pricing sync with Karthik (sales) to lock committed throughput and acceptance criteria.
- Day 11–21: Evidence handoff: SOC2 and engineering runbook for audit trails.
- Day 22–30: DocuSign-ready package and mutual sign-off (can accelerate if legal redlines are light).

Irene — can you confirm whether the DPA exceptions Cardinal flagged on the call (data residency range and subprocessor notifications) are likely to be accept/reject or if we can offer compensating controls (e.g., contractual commitments + regional routing)?

Karthik — will assemble the order form pricing buckets (pilot: 50 TPS burst, limited prod commit: 1M tokens/mo) and the acceptance checklist that Emma requested. I'll own coordination and the MAP timeline.

If Cardinal can confirm procurement contact for contract execution (DocuSign account or person), we will route the final package to them directly.

Cheers,
Markus Klein
Director, Strategic Accounts | Redwood Inference
markus_klein@redwood.com
attachments: OrderForm_Draft_v3.docx

From: procurement@cardinalhealth.com
To: markus_klein@redwood.com
Cc: Emma Liao <emma.liao@cardinalhealth.com>
Date: 2026-06-16T08:37:00-07:00
Subject: Re: MAP & timeline proposal for pilot -> production (Cardinal)

Markus —

Thanks — procurement reviewed the OrderForm_Draft_v3.docx and returned a short list of commercial questions and a few redlines:
- Need a clear clause for rollback/rollback costs if acceptance fails after production cutover
- Request explicit SLA tiers for latency (p50/p95) tied to committed throughput
- We will propose a 30-day warranty/acceptance period and an escrow-like clause for data export in the event of termination

We also asked legal for the preferred DocuSign account info (we use procurement@cardinalhealth.com as our signing gate). We will provide annotated redline PDF by COB tomorrow.

Procurement note: timeline is firm because internal audit will rely on the signed DPA + SOC2 evidence to allow live traffic after the acceptance window. If legal holds past 3 weeks, we will need to consider an interim carve-out (pilot-only sandbox) rather than production.

Regards,
Cardinal Health Procurement
attachments: CH_OrderForm_Questions.pdf

From: markus_klein@redwood.com
To: karthik_iyer, irene_choi, olga_petrov
Date: 2026-06-18T16:23:00-07:00
Subject: INTERNAL: next steps on Cardinal MAP & legal sequencing

Team —

Recap and owners after procurement's note:
1) Irene: prioritize DPA redlines (data residency + subprocessors). Aim to produce a DPA mark-up call-out doc (must/optional list) by EOD 6/19. We may offer conditional regional routing and a 3rd-party subprocessor disclosure cadence as compensating controls.
2) Karthik: finalize order-form pricing buckets + SLA language (latency slices) by 6/20 so we can roll pricing into the DocuSign package. Draft acceptance checklist needs to map to the 30-day window (test scripts + sample traces).
3) Olga: prepare the SOC2 evidence handoff pack and a short engineering note describing KV cache behavior and request trace retention (one-pager).
4) Me: consolidate and drive the MAP; I will own the hubspot deal record and the DocuSign routing.

Risk / contingency: procurement flagged that if legal overruns 3 weeks we lose the chance to go to limited production in the intended window. Prepare a fallback: 'pilot-only' carve-out that allows sandbox traffic with strict data segmentation and no PHI. We will surface this to Emma as an alternative next week if needed.

Please reply in thread with any blockers. I will sync with Emma on Monday morning (6/21) with a consolidated package.

- Markus
